scope: Second pass through backend input validation, immutable storage/retry durability, authentication, transaction/lease recovery, backup handling and optional ghost presentation. Four additional gaps were reproduced and fixed locally.

findings.title: Stored JSON validation missed exponent overflow and differed across providers
findings.before: A blob with a matching SHA256 and {"coordinate":1e400} decoded to infinity. S3/GCS also used permissive JSON decoders.
findings.after: A shared pure JSON parser checks finite floats, duplicate keys, valid Unicode and depth. Local storage, S3, GCS and archive/restore all use the same integrity decoder. HTTP's existing 1,200,000-node/depth limits remain; stored byte-bounded canonical expansions retain their allowance. Iterator traversal uses memory proportional to depth.
tests: test_stored_json_rejects_invalid_data_even_with_matching_hash: three providers, compressed/plain and five invalid trees

findings.title: Immutable retries could acknowledge a file whose publication flush failed
findings.before: After the final name was linked and directory sync raised OSError, a retry returned the existing digest even while the same durability error persisted.
findings.after: Reuse verifies the object and repeats root/shard directory sync before acknowledgement. Continued flush failures stay retryable failures; recovery returns the same digest without replacing or duplicating the object.
findings.limit: Injected directory-sync failure and successful retry were tested. Physical power-loss behavior on the deployment filesystem was not tested.

findings.title: Unicode normalization could overflow the database username-key column
findings.before: The accepted 40-character name U+FDFA repeated 40 times expands to a 720-character NFKC comparison key; PostgreSQL allows 160.
findings.after: Display-name validation checks normalized comparison length before a database write. Profile changes/new sign-ins reject these names with 422 and retain the original profile. Ordinary Unicode names and collision comparison rules remain.

findings.title: Finite ghost data could exceed renderable geometry ranges
findings.before: The server and client accepted 1e300 in a ghost pose; finiteness of a double does not make it a valid Vector3 component.
findings.after: The server drops optional poses outside the existing broad 100,000-component safety range while still accepting valid timing proof. The client applies the same bound before rendering, including recordings saved by older servers.
